source.title: Active Avoidance: Neural Mechanisms and Attenuation of Pavlovian Conditioned Responding.

confidence_rationale: Human fMRI dissociating active avoidance from yoked extinction: instrumental control engages the striatum at shock-omission and PERSISTENTLY diminishes threat, including transfer to novel stimuli. This is direct human evidence for a response-produced safety/relief credit attached to a SPECIFIC avoidance action -- the MECH-358 safety half and the SD-059 'response-produced safety' wiring. Human data (preferred over rodent), within-paradigm contrast; confidence held below 0.8 because BOLD-at-omission is a correlational read of 'credit', not a per-action-class table.
failure_signatures: Yoked extinction (matched shock, no instrumental control) did NOT confer the persistent threat reduction -- absent an action-contingent credit signal, mere safety exposure fails, matching SD-059's prediction that a global 'avoidance works' scalar without an affordance-indexed action credit is insufficient.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In humans, exercising instrumental control over an aversive stimulus (active avoidance) engages striatal BOLD responses to shock omission and persistently attenuates conditioned threat responding -- more durably than yoked extinction -- and reduces subsequent threat conditioning to novel cues.
mapping.ree_translation: The striatal shock-omission response is the response-produced safety credit that MECH-358's SAFETY half writes when a directed action terminates the threat (threat_scale<=0 -> credit safety_affordance[class]). The persistence/transfer maps to SD-059 tagging the credited first-action class as an escape affordance approachable under future threat. The yoked-extinction null maps to why MECH-357's global scalar is not enough.
mapping.mapping_caveat: fMRI BOLD at omission indexes a credit-like signal at the circuit level but does not demonstrate the per-first-action-class EMA table or the threat-gated approach bonus that are the specific computational content of MECH-358; the action-credit is inferred, not isolated to discrete action classes.
mapping.source_context: Healthy human adults; threat conditioning then active avoidance vs yoked extinction; skin conductance + BOLD; next-day novel threat conditioning.

confidence_components.notes: Human within-subject design lowers transfer risk relative to rodent work; mapping fidelity good for the safety-half but does not reach the per-action-class table.
